newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
A National Action Plan for employment of women at all levels including top management positions is going to be taken up shortly, government officials said on Sunday.
The government and tribal leaders were very close to a solution of the staggering problems in Chittagong Hill Tracts, a ruling party MP from Rangamati hill district said in the parliament on Sunday.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Sunday that the government would take all possible steps for mordernining the airforce and procrement of latest aircraft.
Toxic chemical wastes, being released by industrial unit, caused the recent fish epidemic in the river Shitalakhya near Dhaka, fisheries officials said.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, now attending the SAARC summit in the Maldives, met with the Indian Prime Minister I K Gujral at Male on Sunday and discussed bilateral issues.
Visiting Director General of FAO, Jacques Diouf, have assured the UN body's continued support for the development of agriculture and rural infrastructure in Bangladesh.
The government has so far received 40 applications for setting up banks in the private sector.
Pran Agriculture Marketing Company Ltd singed a joint venture deal with Indian firm, Tera-Pak, for setting up a plant for producing quality fruit juices.
